newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil Mar/Apr spread widens.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil Mar/Apr spread widens.

text.p: Singapore front month gas oil swaps firmed on expectations of fresh support from some players who are pricing out to Indonesia which has led to a widening of the March/April backwardation, traders said.
"I think the market firmed because of some pricing to Indonesia and March is quite tight," one trader said
March swaps were last quoted at $25.20/$25.30 per barrel, up from $25.00/$25.10 on Thursday.
The market traded at least twice at $24.85 per barrel this morning, but in the afternoon it was traded up with deals done at $25.05, $25.10, $25.15 and $25.20, brokers said.
The March/April time spread widened due to the expected arrival of aribtrage cargoes from the West in Europe. The spread traded at 65 cents in the morning and at 75 cents in the afternoon.
March/April was last quoted at 75/85 cents, brokers said.
Jet fuel is holding its own at the higher level on the return of buying interest from a local trader who is believed to be looking to cover commitments to Indonesia.
March regrade or jet fuel/gas oil spread were last quoted at $1.40/$1.80 per barrel up about 20 cents from Thursday.
Fuel oil continued to come under selling pressure on fears of an oversupply in the local market as players put together arbitrage cargoes from the West to the region.

Amid poor demand from China, residual fuel stocks in Singapore rose by 1.974-million-barrel for the week ended February 28 to a nine-month high of 12.299 million barrels, Singapore's Trade Development Board said Thursday.
March fuel oil swaps traded earlier today at $98.00 per tonne down from late Thursday's traded low of $99.00, brokers said.
The market was last quoted at $97.50/$98.50, they said.
The naphtha market were quoted down sharply following big falls in the Japanese market. March was last quoted at $23.00/$23.30 per barrel from Thursday's $23.55/$23.75.
